title: basic-auth gateway secret, model-definition and endpoint validators: authorize the proto-bound ids, and attach has its own validator because its body uses singular model_config
answers: Why does creating a gateway endpoint with camelCase modelConfigs require USE on the referenced model definitions?
Which validator authorizes attaching a model to a gateway endpoint, and what does it check?
Where is the USE check for secret_id on gateway model-definition create and update?
Why does attach to a gateway endpoint require UPDATE on the endpoint and USE on the model definition?
Creating a gateway model definition with secretId only: is the secret permission still enforced?
body:
Path: Basic-auth validators for gateway writes that link secrets or model definitions in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py: model-definition create and update (secret_id), endpoint create and update (model_configs), and endpoint model attach (singular model_config). They decide USE on the referenced secret or model definitions before the handler links them.
Rule: Read the authorized ids from the proto parse, via _get_request_message(<ProtoClass>()), not from body.get("secret_id") or body.get("model_configs"). Endpoint create and update use _model_configs_from_request. AttachModelToGatewayEndpoint maps to validate_can_attach_model_to_gateway_endpoint, which requires UPDATE on the endpoint and USE on model_config.model_definition_id. Do not reuse validate_can_update_gateway_endpoint for attach, because UpdateGatewayEndpoint has no model_config field and would check no model definition.
Symptom: A camelCase-only body (secretId, modelConfigs) was invisible to the raw-key read, so the USE check was skipped while the handler still linked the secret or model definitions. Attach was checked against an update validator that never read model_config, so the referenced model definition was not checked.
Constraints: A model-definition create with no secret id is allowed and left to the handler. An update that does not change the secret returns True after the endpoint permission check. Basic-auth app only.
applies: Basic-auth authorization for gateway model-definition create/update, endpoint create/update, and the endpoints/models/attach route in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py.
says: Users can attach models to gateway endpoints without permission to use those models.
Prevent members from linking saved credentials when configuring a gateway model definition.
Attaching a model to a deployed endpoint should require use rights on that model.
Endpoints are being created with model definitions that the creator cannot access.
search: Basic-auth gateway validators in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py for model-definition create/update (validate_can_create_gateway_model_definition, validate_can_update_gateway_model_definition), endpoint create/update (validate_can_create_gateway_endpoint, validate_can_update_gateway_endpoint), and endpoint model attach authorize referenced secret and model IDs by reading parsed protobuf messages via _get_request_message(<ProtoClass>()). Endpoint create and update use _model_configs_from_request, while AttachModelToGatewayEndpoint maps to validate_can_attach_model_to_gateway_endpoint requiring UPDATE on the endpoint and USE on model_config.model_definition_id. Do not reuse validate_can_update_gateway_endpoint for attach because UpdateGatewayEndpoint lacks the singular model_config field and skips model definition checks. Model-definition create with no secret_id is allowed, and update without changing the secret returns True after checking endpoint permissions.
